reviewType: independent AI sense-aware residual new-owner/prior-canonical collision audit
scope: All 22 current proposed-new source sentences whose full source text matches a prior canonical target detector in the all-discovered audit
method: Read collision tool output, source inventory, current editorial decisions and prior canonical brief/target meanings; distinguish incidental matches in other source spans from same-target matches and compare shared strings by construction and sense. Regex match alone was never treated as ownership proof.

records.sourceExample: Guests should show up before noon.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: The new source is arrival before noon; 364 teaches being present to support someone. Same words, different learner decision. Keep sense-specific ownership.

records.sourceExample: Our timing is too tight if we rely on the final train.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: The prior detector matches the separate subordinate phrase rely on the final train. The proposed tight-schedule phrase is a different span and meaning.

records.sourceExample: I packed the documents so everything was ready to go.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: The source uses packed as a literal verb for documents; 434 teaches a crowded venue. Ready to go is the proposed readiness target.

records.sourceExample: Her argument was grounded in facts rather than speculation.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: Evidence-based argument versus feeling emotionally steady and connected to daily reality. The shared adjective is not a shared lesson outcome.

records.sourceExample: The opening scene should pull them in at once.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: The prior detector matches the separate at once adjunct, which here means immediately; 048 focuses simultaneous demands. Pull them in teaches attracting an audience.

records.sourceExample: A short reply may come across as rude.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: Impression-giving come across as differs from 120's chance-discovery come across. The shorter 120 detector matches inside the new construction, so aliasing must be sense- and construction-aware.

records.sourceExample: The film relied on star power to fill cinemas.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: Relied on is a separate ordinary dependency verb in the source. Star power names the celebrity's audience draw.

records.proposedPhrase: keep your feet on the ground
records.sourceExample: It is wise to keep your feet on the ground after a big win.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: The longer phrase means remain realistic after success, not 536's local operational conditions; the latter is a substring collision.

records.sourceExample: The schedule ended up running their life.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: Ended up is a separate eventual-result expression in the sentence; running their life describes control over daily choices.

records.sourceExample: The effects will show up in the final results.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: Effects becoming evident in final results differs from 364's human supportive presence. Exact-title collision needs an explicit sense tag.

records.sourceExample: Teenagers can become caught up in social pressure online.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: Becoming entangled in social pressure differs from 1521's catching up through conversation after time apart.

records.sourceExample: An unknown artist can blow up overnight online.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: The matched adverb overnight contributes speed, but the proposed construction also teaches blow up as sudden online popularity. They are not interchangeable target units.

records.sourceExample: Do not read serious claims with your brain switched off.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: Reading claims with one's brain switched off means inattentive or uncritical thinking. Canonical 375 teaches deliberately leaving work/worries mentally for relaxation; the subject, context and valence differ. Preserve this distinction in the future lesson brief.

records.sourceExample: Officials have their hands on the wheel during a crisis.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: Direct control during a crisis differs from practical hands-on participation; a space/hyphen tolerant detector caused this false semantic match.

records.sourceExample: The celebration is not worth picking up the pieces afterwards.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: Recovering from damage after an extravagant celebration is the idiom pick up the pieces, not 441's informally acquiring knowledge. The prior detector matches only the two-word prefix. A future lesson should make the financial or practical damage concrete because the source sentence alone does not specify it.

records.sourceExample: She is even-tempered under pressure.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: Even-tempered is a stable calm disposition; canonical 486 under pressure names the stressful circumstance and its source occurrence is a separate adjunct, not the proposed adjective.

records.sourceExample: The plan was falling apart after the second delay.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: A plan breaking down after delays is not canonical 1164, which teaches a person becoming too upset to cope. Canonical 098 adds the fixed idiom at the seams and 521 narrows to practical basics; the present bare phrasal verb can own plan failure if the future lesson makes the object/sense explicit.

records.sourceExample: Her parents have her best interests at heart.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: Best interests at heart is the fixed welfare-motive construction. Canonical 562 at heart teaches underlying nature, a different construction and sense.

records.sourceExample: The device gathered dust once the novelty wears off.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: Novelty wears off means initial appeal fades. The source also says gathered dust, which is separately owned by canonical 1056 and means an item remains unused; two effects can coexist.

records.sourceExample: Children grow out of clothes remarkably quickly.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: Children literally becoming too big for clothes is distinct from canonical 957, where a design develops from real daily life.

records.sourceExample: A traditional product need not be stuck in the past.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: Stuck in the past means unable to move beyond old ways. Canonical 131 stick in my mind means remain memorable; stem overlap is not semantic overlap.

records.sourceExample: A festival changes shape when it enters a new culture.
records.classification: distinct target construction/sense or separate source span; retain provisional new proposal
records.reason: Changes shape means takes a different form across cultures. Canonical 020 shape is an influence verb that affects how something develops; changed form is distinct. Canonical 759 take shape means begin to form, also different.

watchItems.note: When authoring, distinguish bare plan-failure fall apart from emotional breakdown owner 1164 and fixed longer constructions 098/521; current source alone does not justify merging into those owners.

limits: This is a sense review of the 22 detector-overlap candidates, not an exhaustive search for all semantic duplicates beyond this candidate set; AI peer review only, not human approval.
